title: A study routine that sticks
description: A routine sticks when it is small, scheduled and kind to miss. Here is how to build one that survives real life.

body.heading: Attach study to a fixed anchor
paragraphs: Vague intentions like 'study more' dissolve under pressure. A routine survives when it is tied to an anchor that already happens: after dinner, before the evening show, first thing on Saturday with coffee.
Choose a modest dose: twenty or thirty minutes is enough to make progress and small enough to start on a tired day. You can always do more; the routine only asks for the dose.

body.heading: Make the start automatic
paragraphs: Decide in advance where you will sit, what you will open first, and what 'starting' looks like. Every decision you remove from the moment is one less chance to negotiate your way out.
End each session by writing the next session's first task on a note. Tomorrow's you will thank today's you for the running start, and the chain of sessions will hold through busy weeks.

takeaway: Anchor a small study dose to a moment that already exists, and prepare each next start.
